summary: Iteration 5 — Scanner.jsx enhancements (P0 tablet camera multi-format + P1 USB plug-and-play scanner) fully verified via Playwright. 10/10 scenarios PASS. Login admin/Admin@123 → /scanner shows 'USB scanner LISTENING' badge by default (data-testid usb-status). Toggle (usb-toggle-btn) flips LISTENING↔OFF correctly. Global window keydown listener captures rapid USB-style keystrokes (10ms delay) on body focus + Enter → POSTs /api/scans exactly once with payload {barcode_value:'RSC-00004', action:'Search', device_type:'USB/Manual'}, toast 'Found: FOUNTAN' shows, page navigates to /catalogs/<id>. Manual input flow (focus scanner-input, type slow 80ms/char, Enter) ALSO fires exactly one /api/scans call — global listener correctly ignores the scanner-input field (no double-fire). Switching action to 'Issue Batch' renders batch-issue-card with basket-count '0 items'; USB-style scan then increments basket-count to '1 item'. Camera Start (camera-start-btn) in headless Chromium gracefully shows camera-error 'No camera detected on this device.' — page does not crash, usb-status badge still visible, Start Camera button still present. After 3 enable/disable toggle pairs, a single USB-style scan still produces exactly 1 /api/scans POST — confirming the global keydown listener is registered ONCE per mount (cleanup works, no duplicate listeners). Code review of /app/frontend/src/pages/Scanner.jsx confirms SUPPORTED_FORMATS array with CODE_128, CODE_39, CODE_93, EAN_13, EAN_8, UPC_A, UPC_E, ITF, CODABAR, DATA_MATRIX, PDF_417, QR_CODE; useBarCodeDetectorIfSupported=true on both Html5Qrcode constructor AND experimentalFeatures; fps=15; dynamic qrbox sized by viewport; videoConstraints requesting 1920x1080 ideal with focusMode:'continuous'. No runtime JS errors during any flow.
critical_code_review_comments: Scanner.jsx (~510 lines): global window keydown listener correctly cleaned up on unmount via removeEventListener — verified by zero duplicate listener firings after multiple toggles. Good use of addToBasketRef pattern so the handler stays stable and only re-registers when usbHotkeyOn changes.

isTypingTarget() check correctly exempts the scanner-input by data-testid AND blocks other text inputs/textareas/contentEditable — verified that manual input does NOT trigger the global handler simultaneously.

Minor enhancement: addToBasket() is the same function used for Search/View/Issue Single/Issue Batch — when USB scanner fires while a Search/View flow is mid-flight (api.post('/scans') awaiting), there's no debounce. If a user double-scans rapidly the same code, two POSTs and two navigations can race. Consider an in-flight ref guard (isScanningRef.current) to prevent overlapping scans, especially relevant for tablets where users tend to over-scan.

USB buffer reset condition: `(now - buf.lastTs) < 500` on Enter requires Enter to follow the last char within 500ms — this is correct, but if the scanner uses a slow Enter terminator, a valid scan could be discarded. 500ms is a safe threshold for typical USB HID scanners (Honeywell, Symbol, Zebra) which terminate within ~30ms; documenting this would help future maintainers.

Camera config: useBarCodeDetectorIfSupported is passed BOTH as a top-level Html5Qrcode constructor option AND inside experimentalFeatures. The library typically reads it from experimentalFeatures only — the top-level key is likely ignored. Not harmful, but redundant; verify with html5-qrcode v2.3+ docs which key it currently honors so we know the native BarcodeDetector path is actually engaged on iPad Safari and Android Chrome (this is the actual fix for the tablet client).

Camera-error UX: 'No camera detected on this device.' is shown for NotFoundError. On a real tablet without granted permission, the error path is NotAllowedError → 'Camera permission denied. Allow it from the address bar lock icon.' — both are present and graceful. Good.

Recommend adding telemetry: log a one-time console.info when BarcodeDetector is actually picked vs. when html5-qrcode falls back to ZXing-WASM — would help diagnose tablet decoding issues remotely without RDP.
seed_data_creation: None — used pre-seeded catalog RSC-00004 (FOUNTAN) fetched via GET /api/catalogs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Scanner.jsx P0 (multi-format camera config) and P1 (USB HID listener) are both verified working in preview. The actual tablet camera decoding fix CANNOT be e2e validated in headless Chromium (no real camera/BarcodeDetector) — it must be smoke-tested by the user on their iPad/Android tablet against an actual fabric label. Code structure is correct: 12 formats configured, native BarcodeDetector enabled, 15fps, dynamic qrbox, 1920x1080 video with continuous focus. For regression: the regex `INTER_CHAR_MS=60ms` and `MIN_LEN=3` constants in the USB keydown handler — DO NOT relax these without re-testing manual input (typing slowly must still work via the dedicated input field, and stray Enter presses must not fire a scan). Recommended next manual test on real tablet: open /scanner over HTTPS, tap Start Camera, point at a printed CODE_128 fabric label, confirm decode + toast + navigation in <2 seconds.
rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: 'camera opens but does not decode on tablet'. RCA from code review: previous Html5Qrcode config likely defaulted to QR_CODE only (or a narrow format set) + ZXing-WASM fallback, which is slow on mobile Safari/Chrome and frequently fails on 1D barcodes printed on glossy/curved fabric labels at <300dpi. Fix correctly addresses this by: (a) explicitly enumerating 12 formats including all 1D codes typically printed on fabric (CODE_128/39/EAN_13), (b) enabling experimentalFeatures.useBarCodeDetectorIfSupported which routes to the browser's NATIVE BarcodeDetector API on iPadOS 16+/Chrome 88+ (orders of magnitude faster + more reliable than WASM), (c) requesting 1920x1080 at 15fps with continuous autofocus (was likely 640x480 / passive focus). The companion P1 feature (global window keydown buffer) adds support for keyboard-emulating USB scanners — verified empirically by simulated rapid keystrokes; the user's plug-and-play USB scanner will now work without requiring focus on the input field.
